name: Infant water / nursery water (if not routed to Category 1 by age-marketing)
anchor: strictest applicable sovereign drinking-water or packaged-water maximum, per litre of finished product as consumed, with the natural-mineral-water product-form split preserved as the governments write it
cross_reference: Powdered and liquid infant formula, and the reconstituted feed, are governed by HMTc Category 1. This row governs the water only.
native_basis_label: as consumed, per litre of nursery water as sold and as used to reconstitute formula (µg/L; numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
scope_note: This row is packaged water as placed on the market and assessed per litre as consumed. It is governed by the packaged-water bridge stated in the category method note: national drinking-water maxima apply because the product is the same substance in the same basis, and because FDA incorporates the EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation MCLs into the bottled-water standard of quality at 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) while the scope of EU Directive 2020/2184 expressly reaches water put into bottles or containers. In scope: purified or distilled water marketed for infants, for mixing with formula or cereal, and for drinking by infants and young children, where the product is water and is not routed to HMTc Category 1 by age-marketing of a formula product. This is the child-protective row of the category. Two basis points are stated explicitly because both are attack surfaces. First, the native basis is per litre of water as sold, which is also the basis in which it is consumed after it is used to reconstitute powdered formula; the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula under the locked method and is NOT applied here, because nursery water is not a powder and applying a reconstitution factor to it would be an invented basis treatment. Second, the reconstituted feed's own contaminant load is governed by the infant-formula standard in Category 1; this row governs only the water contributed to it, and the two must not be conflated or double-counted.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(dry weight|dry matter|dehydrated|migration|leach|material content|surface|\bfeed\b|fat basis))(?=.*(water|as[ _]?consumed|mg/l|placed on market|food as listed)).*$
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary per-litre / as-consumed water or food-schedule basis. The guard rejects dry-weight, dehydrated, migration/leachate, article material-content and feed bases outright, so a dry-commodity maximum level or a food-contact migration limit can never anchor a per-litre water cell. It admits mg/kg-expressed food-schedule rows (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011) because potable water density is within 0.3 per cent of 1 kg/L, so µg/kg and µg/L are the same number to well inside analytical uncertainty; that is a stated identity, not a silent conversion.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; strictest applicable sovereign maximum for the exact packaged-water form in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, control where no defensible sovereign number exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Pb.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for packaged drinking water; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
Pb.substantiation: Lead at 5 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum and it is corroborated four ways: the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, the FDA bottled-water allowable level at 21 CFR 165.110 (0.005 mg/L), the Health Canada maximum acceptable concentration and the NHMRC health-based guideline value. The Directive's 5 µg/L is its end-state value, which member states must meet by 12 January 2036 and below which the transitional value of 10 µg/L applies until then; HMTc adopts the end-state value now, so this cell is stricter than currently-enforced EU practice, but the FDA value of 5 µg/L is in force today and is independently sufficient to compel the number. The looser 10 µg/L values (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, the WHO provisional guideline value, and the Codex/mineral-water family) are named in the candidate set and are not selected because the method takes the strictest applicable value. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: HMTc's standing rule is that where an infant-specific instrument is stricter than the general one it binds. That check was run for every cell on this row and no infant instrument is stricter for lead. EU Regulation 2023/915 sets 10 µg/kg for liquid infant and follow-on formula placed on the market (eu2023_pb_formula_liquid_10) and 20 µg/kg for ready-to-use drinks for infants and young children (eu2023_pb_infant_drinks_ready_20); Codex sets 10 µg/kg for infant formula as consumed (codex_pb_infant-formula-formula-for-special-medic_10); the UK, Canada, China, Israel, Brazil, Korea, Thailand, Singapore, GSO and Hong Kong infant-formula-as-consumed values are all 10 µg/kg. All are looser than the 5 µg/L drinking-water anchor selected here, so the drinking-water family is itself the child-protective anchor and no infant instrument is adopted.

Cd.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cd.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (NHMRC health-based guideline value); stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
Cd.substantiation: Cadmium at 2 µg/L is the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines health-based guideline value (0.002 mg/L), the strictest cadmium maximum any government sets for water. It is applied under the packaged-water bridge stated in the category method note: the product is the same substance in the same per-litre as-consumed basis, and the guideline carries no packaged-product carve-out. The next tier is 3 µg/L (WHO, Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013), then 5 µg/L (EU Drinking Water Directive, FDA 21 CFR 165.110, EPA MCL, California), then 7 µg/L (Health Canada). All are named in the candidate set; none is selected because 2 µg/L is applicable and stricter. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: the infant-specific cadmium instruments are looser — EU Regulation 2023/915 sets 5 µg/kg for liquid cow-milk-based formula (eu2023_cd_formula_cow_liquid_5), 10 µg/kg for liquid soy-based formula (eu2023_cd_formula_soy_liquid_10) and 20 µg/kg for ready-to-use infant drinks (eu2023_cd_infant_drinks_ready_20); Israel sets 5 µg/kg for ready-to-eat infant and toddler formula. The 2 µg/L drinking-water value is stricter than all of them and is adopted.

tAs.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
tAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
tAs.substantiation: Total arsenic at 10 µg/L is unanimous across every applicable instrument in the pool: EU Drinking Water Directive, FDA 21 CFR 165.110, the EPA MCL adopted into the bottled-water standard of quality by reference, California, Health Canada, NHMRC, Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 and the WHO provisional guideline value. There is no stricter sovereign total-arsenic value for water anywhere in the register. Total arsenic is published as its own cell and is not satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: no jurisdiction sets a total-arsenic maximum for infant formula below the drinking-water value. The infant-scoped total-arsenic instruments in the register are India's 50 µg/kg for infant milk substitutes and infant foods (in_tas_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_50), Singapore's 100 µg/kg for infant formula (sg_foodregs_2026_infant_formula_tas_100) and Israel's 1000 µg/kg for ready-to-eat infant and toddler formula; all are looser than the 10 µg/L value adopted here.

iAs.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
iAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for the exact product form; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic at 6 µg/L is the Israel FCS 2016 maximum level for the exact product form ('Bottled drinking water and mineral water', source row 16.1, 0.006 mg/kg), the strictest sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum for packaged water in the register. The alternatives are the US EPA drinking-water MCL recorded as inorganic arsenic at 10 µg/L and the Chilean Decreto 977/1996 Article 160 value of 10 µg/L for mineral and packaged drinking waters; both are named and neither is selected because 6 µg/L is applicable and stricter. The species cell is retained separately from total arsenic even though arsenic in potable water is effectively all inorganic, because the HMTc panel never allows a species to satisfy a total: a lot must clear both 10 µg/L total arsenic and 6 µg/L inorganic arsenic. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: EU Regulation 2023/915 sets inorganic arsenic at 10 µg/kg for liquid infant formula (eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10), Israel at 10 µg/kg for ready-to-eat infant and toddler formula and Brazil at 20 µg/kg for infant formulas. All are looser than the 6 µg/L value adopted here.

tHg.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
tHg.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
tHg.substantiation: Total mercury at 1 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum, set independently by the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B, the NHMRC health-based guideline, the Health Canada maximum acceptable concentration (which the source table states applies to all forms of mercury) and the Israel FCS 2016 packaged-water line. The FDA bottled-water allowable level and the California MCL are 2 µg/L and the Vietnamese bottled-water value is 6 µg/L; all are named and none is selected. Total mercury is published as a total and is never satisfied by a methylmercury or inorganic-mercury result. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: the only infant-specific mercury instrument in the pool is the Israeli value of 4 µg/kg for ready-to-eat infant and toddler formula (il_fcs2016_thg_14_infant_and_toddler_formulas_ready_to_eat_4), four times looser than the 1 µg/L value adopted here.

MeHg.rationale: Mercury in sealed packaged drinking water is present essentially as inorganic Hg(II). Methylation is a microbial process requiring anaerobic sulfate- or iron-reducing activity in sediment or biota; it does not occur in a treated, filtered, disinfected and sealed packaged-water matrix, and there is no aquatic food chain in the product to bioaccumulate methylmercury. Methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so it is bounded by identity at the published total-mercury ceiling of 1 µg/L. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Methylmercury is not separately quantified as a routine cell. Total mercury is measured on every certification lot by cold-vapour atomic fluorescence or ICP-MS against the published total-mercury ceiling. Where a lot result reaches or exceeds half the total-mercury ceiling, speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is run as a reflex and the source water is investigated; a detectable methyl fraction is an immediate non-conformance regardless of the total-mercury result.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water. Every drinking-water and packaged-water instrument in the pool regulates mercury as total mercury with no methyl line, and Hong Kong Cap 132V regulates the packaged-drinking-water mercury cell as INORGANIC mercury (0.006 mg/kg, hk_cap132v_ihg_bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters-other-than-natural_6), which is direct sovereign confirmation that the regulated mercury species in packaged water is the inorganic one. The only methylmercury maxima anywhere in the register are fish and aquatic-animal limits (for example fda_cpg540600_mehg_fish_1000), which govern a bioaccumulating tissue matrix and have no application to water.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I; EU Commission Directive 2003/40/EC (natural mineral waters); US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110; California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431; Health Canada Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality (2025 summary tables); NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines; WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality; Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2; Israel FCS 2016; India FSSAI 2016; Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011; GSO 193/2021; Colombia Res 4506/2013; Chile Decreto 977/1996; Fiji FSR 2009.

Ni.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Ni.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
Ni.substantiation: Nickel at 20 µg/L is the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, matched exactly by the NHMRC health-based guideline and by the Hong Kong Cap 132V natural-mineral-waters line. The looser candidates are Hong Kong's 70 µg/L for other packaged drinking waters, the WHO guideline value of 70 µg/L, and 100 µg/L from FDA 21 CFR 165.110 and California; all are named and none is selected. The FDA and California nickel values descend from an EPA nickel MCL that was remanded in 1995, which is a further reason not to treat 100 µg/L as the operative ceiling when a current statutory value of 20 µg/L is applicable. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: EU Regulation 2024/1987 sets nickel at 100 µg/kg for liquid infant and young-child formula (eu2024_ni_formula_liquid_100), 250 µg/kg for non-soy powder and 400 µg/kg for soy-isolate powder; all are looser than the 20 µg/L value adopted here.

Sn.rationale: No sovereign sets a tin maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water. The drinking-water instrument family carries no tin parameter at all (EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I Parts B and C; US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110 standards of quality; Health Canada; NHMRC; WHO), and none of the national food-schedule packaged-water lines (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Chile Decreto 977/1996, Fiji FSR 2009) carries a tin entry for water. A read-across is not supportable: the nearest sovereign tin maxima are the canned-food and canned-beverage maximum levels, which exist to bound dissolution of tin from a tinplate container wall into an acidic canned matrix, and the canned-beverage value (100 mg/kg inorganic tin) sits roughly four orders of magnitude above anything a packaged water can plausibly contain, so importing it would publish a ceiling that functions as no limit at all. The dominant packaging for this category (PET, HDPE, glass, aluminium) contains no tin. Nursery water is sold in PET or HDPE gallon and litre containers; there is no tinplate presentation of this form. Tin therefore remains a mandatory control cell; no number is invented.
Sn.reference_method: Tin by ICP-MS on the finished packaged product in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, on every certification lot, reported against the method limit of quantification rather than a ceiling. Any quantifiable tin result triggers investigation of the container, closure and liner, the filling line and the source water, and lot release is withheld pending root-cause identification and a clean re-test. Where the product is presented in a tinplate or tin-coated container, the EU canned-beverage inorganic-tin maximum level recorded as the companion instrument applies as a regulatory hard stop in addition to this control.

Al.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Al.label: strictest applicable sovereign value; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked; an indicator / secondary / aesthetic parameter, disclosed as such
Al.substantiation: Aluminium at 200 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign value and is disclosed here as a non-health-based parameter rather than a toxicological line: it is an Annex I Part C INDICATOR parameter in the EU Drinking Water Directive, a SECONDARY (aesthetically based) allowable level at FDA 21 CFR 165.110, and an AESTHETIC guideline for acid-soluble aluminium in the NHMRC guidelines. The health-based alternatives are far looser (Health Canada's maximum acceptable concentration of 2900 µg/L; California's MCL of 1000 µg/L), so adopting 200 µg/L is the strictest applicable treatment and is materially protective. Its aesthetic derivation is stated rather than concealed because the label of the parameter, not only its number, is part of the provenance. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: the only infant-specific aluminium maxima in the register are the FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19 values of 500 µg/kg for infant formula and follow-on formula (aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500) and 1000 µg/kg for soy-based infant formula (aunz_sch19_al_formula_soy_1000). Both are looser than the 200 µg/L packaged-water parameter adopted here, so the packaged-water value is itself the child-protective one. No infant instrument is adopted and no exposure or occurrence reasoning enters this cell.

Cr.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cr.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
Cr.substantiation: Total chromium at 25 µg/L is the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, the strictest applicable sovereign maximum; it is the Directive's end-state value, to be met by 12 January 2036, with a transitional value of 50 µg/L in force until then. The 50 µg/L tier (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Health Canada, WHO, California) and the 100 µg/L tier (EPA MCL, FDA 21 CFR 165.110) are named and not selected. This cell is published as a FIRM limit rather than as a screen, which is a deliberate departure from the HMTc default for total chromium and is compelled by the instruments themselves: in a food matrix total chromium is dominated by nutritionally benign Cr(III) and is a poor proxy for the health-relevant species, but the drinking-water instruments regulate total chromium precisely because the two species interconvert in aqueous media, and the Health Canada entry states in terms that the maximum acceptable concentration protects against chromium(VI) effects and is established for total chromium. The hexavalent species is not displaced: it is published separately at 10 µg/L. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: no jurisdiction sets a chromium maximum for infant formula, infant drinks or infant foods below the drinking-water value; the nearest infant-adjacent chromium instrument in the register is China's 2000 µg/kg for milk and modified milk powder (cn_crtotal_milk-powder-and-modified-milk-powder-gen_2000), eighty times looser than the 25 µg/L value adopted here.

Cr-VI.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cr-VI.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
Cr-VI.substantiation: Hexavalent chromium at 10 µg/L is the California State Water Resources Control Board Title 22 section 64431 Table 64431-A maximum contaminant level (0.01 mg/L), re-adopted in 2024 after health-risk and feasibility analysis. It is the only enforceable hexavalent-chromium drinking-water maximum set by any government in the register; the sole alternative is the NHMRC guideline that hexavalent chromium should not exceed 50 µg/L, which is named and not selected. California is a sub-national government, so the selection is disclosed as such: it is adopted because it is a binding, enforceable governmental maximum for the same substance in the same basis and because it is the strictest applicable, not because it is federal. HMTc publishes Cr-VI as its own cell in addition to total chromium; a hexavalent result never satisfies the total-chromium cell and a total-chromium result never satisfies this one. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: no jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any infant food or infant beverage. The only stricter hexavalent-chromium values anywhere in the register are the EU Toy Safety Directive migration limits for accessible toy material and for pacifiers and soothers reached via mouthing; those are migration limits on an article, not dietary maxima on an ingested liquid, they are excluded by this row's basis guard, and importing one would be exactly the basis conflation the method forbids.
